key_insight: SAGE-PINN encodes axisymmetric cylindrical geometry and conservation laws directly into a PINN, removing the coordinate singularity at the axis while jointly learning coupled flow and heat transfer.
engineering_relevance: This enables mesh-free, physics-constrained simulation of stenosed artery nanofluid flow in cylindrical coordinates without case-specific tuning, which is useful for biomedical and other axisymmetric multiphysics designs.
method: Uses parity-preserving variable $s=r^2$ and a modified stream-function to eliminate explicit $1/r$ singular terms.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly with boundary-fitted analytical ansätze.
Stabilizes training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, and Péclet-/Richardson-number continuation.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions, achieving single-precision mass conservation and central-range errors of about 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-driven slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
